forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Gosport sells White Horse Inn for £140,000 to help meet two-year savings target
news_drafts.lead: Gosport Borough Council is disposing of the White Horse Inn freehold for £140,000, a sale explicitly linked to the council's need to deliver savings over the next two financial years. The property currently generates only £135 a year in rental income under a fixed lease, making it a poor-performing asset. The agreed price significantly exceeds the council's March 2025 valuation of £32,000, reflecting the value created by combining the freehold and leasehold interests. The capital receipt from the sale must be used to repay the council's borrowing or fund new capital assets, in accordance with the council's capital strategy. The sale comes as the council forecasts a minor revenue overspend of £23,000 on its £15.2 million net budget in the first quarter of 2026/27—less than 1 per cent variance—while its £38.4 million capital programme faces £8.4 million of slippage, primarily in regeneration schemes including the Local Regeneration Fund projects.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A General Fund Capital Programme 202627 - 203031
findings.headline: £4 million unsupported borrowing adds to council's debt burden
findings.detail: The capital programme allocates £4,006,528 of unsupported borrowing (external borrowing outside PWLB facilities), with £3,780,325 (9% of 2026/27 capital budget) required in the current year. Unsupported borrowing typically carries higher costs than PWLB borrowing and represents additional financial liability not captured in traditional council borrowing metrics.
findings.matters: A lender needs visibility of all external borrowing to assess total debt burden and affordability. Unsupported borrowing at higher cost reduces financial headroom and increases the risk of affordability pressure if service income falls.

findings.paper_title: Appendix A General Fund Capital Programme 202627 - 203031
findings.headline: Levelling Up Fund – Rumstore scheme budget increased 66% from original estimate
findings.detail: The Levelling Up Fund – Rumstore regeneration scheme increased from original 2026/27 budget of £6.04m to current budget of £10.02m. Waterfront Regeneration similarly increased by 26%. The two Levelling Up Fund schemes (Rumstore and Public Realm) together form £16.5m or 37% of the entire capital programme. Budget escalations of this scale suggest cost inflation, scope changes, or inadequate initial estimates.
findings.matters: A lender needs assurance of cost control on major projects. Escalations of 26–66% on large externally-funded schemes indicate planning risk, and heavy dependence on time-limited government grant funding creates delivery risk if grants are withdrawn or conditions change.
findings.figures: Rumstore: original £6,041,000 to current £10,015,935 (increase of £3,974,935, or 66%). Waterfront: original £4,182,000 to current £5,271,080 (increase of 26%).

findings.paper_title: Appendix A General Fund Capital Programme 202627 - 203031
findings.headline: £7 million (16% of capital programme) marked unfunded, concentrated in 2028/29
findings.detail: The programme includes £7,030,000 listed under 'Funding to be Sourced TBC'. The bulk is required in 2028/29 (£6,047,000), with additional amounts in 2026/27 (£602,000) and 2029/30 (£381,000). The single largest component is the Alverstoke Coastal Flood & Erosion scheme (£5.5m of its £8.4m total marked TBC), followed by Beach Management Plan (£1.5m of £1.8m TBC).
findings.matters: A lender assessing a council's financial planning needs to see how major capital commitments will be funded. Having one-sixth of a capital programme without identified funding sources indicates incomplete planning and creates delivery risk.

findings.paper_title: PO Board Report - Q1 Financial Monitoring
findings.headline: Council reports no overspent capital schemes to date despite £38.4m capital programme.
findings.detail: Despite significant capital programme reprofiling and multiple in-year changes, the Council reports that no capital schemes have overspent their budgets. This indicates maintained cost discipline and project management controls across a substantial and complex capital programme.
findings.matters: Positive indicator of capital budget control and project delivery discipline, despite large programme size and complexity with external funding dependencies.
findings.figures: £38.4m capital programme; zero capital scheme overspends reported
findings.quote: To date the Council, have no overspent schemes.

findings.paper_title: PO Board Report - Q1 Financial Monitoring
findings.headline: £2.2m of historic unspent Disabled Facilities Grant monies now properly recorded in capital programme.
findings.detail: The Housing Board capital programme now includes £2.2m of historic unspent Disabled Facilities Grant (DFG) monies that were previously omitted from the approved Capital Programme. This addition corrects the record to show the true amount of ringfenced resources available to the Council.
findings.matters: Clarifies the Council's true capital resource position and demonstrates governance transparency around ringfenced funding that was previously not formally accounted for.
findings.quote: The Housing Board programme has also seen additional slippage of £2.2m linked to historic unspent Disabled Facilities Grant monies that was previously omitted from the approved Capital Programme.
